articles.headline: Charleston Correspondence
articles.author: R. H. Cain
articles.summary: Letter dated Charleston, S.C., July 22, 1865, on the work of the A.M.E. mission in South Carolina. In passing it reports that 'Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs, of Philadelphia,' is on his way to Charleston to look after the Presbyterian Church of that place.
people: of Philadelphia, on his way to Charleston for the Presbyterian Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter from Charleston
articles.author: E. J. Adams
articles.summary: Letter dated Charleston, July 26, 1865. 'Rev. Mr. Cain, late of Brooklyn, and Rev. J. C. Gibbs of Philadelphia, arrived here a week ago.' Mr. Gibbs has entered upon his duties at Zion Church, sent down as agent for the General Assembly (O. S.).
people: of Philadelphia; at Zion Church, Charleston, agent of the General Assembly, O. S. (Rev.)

articles.headline: Editorial Correspondence. Our Visit to Cape Island [Concluded]
articles.summary: Dated Cape Island, July 26. The editor (Elisha Weaver) describes the colored visitors at the Cape. On Wednesday morning James Rodgers of Baltimore had a girl, Maria Cornette of Frederick, Md., brought to the United States Hotel and jailed on a charge of stealing a diamond ring worth $100; 'Rev. Stephen Smith ... at once proceeded to the Mayor and entered bail,' and she was taken to the Banneker House.
people: entered bail for Maria Cornette at Cape Island; visited Captain Williams's farm with his family (Rev.)
gave a 'Reading' in the A.M.E. Church, Cape Island (Mr.)
holds meetings at Cape Island; his Quarterly Meeting July 30 (Rev.)
preached at Cape Island, 4 p.m., July 30 (Rev.)
preached at night, July 30, and asked $50 for the church debt (Bishop)

articles.headline: The Christian Recorder: An Appeal to our Ministers, Members and Friends
articles.summary: Standing appeal of the Book Steward offering the paper to January 1, 1866 for $1.75 (tagged July 1, 8t). Repeats weekly.

articles.headline: Notice (Pauline Medora Green)
articles.summary: 'Pauline Medora Green will hear something to her advantage by calling at No. 613, Barclay street, Philadelphia, Pa.'
people: sought; to call at No. 613 Barclay street, Philadelphia

articles.headline: Notice (harvest home, Buckingham Mountain)
articles.author: Jacob Jay
articles.summary: 'There will be a harvest home held on Buckingham Mountain, five miles from Lambertville Station, on the Belvidere Railroad, ten miles from Attleborough, Pa., on Thursday, August 10th, 1865. Tickets to be had on the ground. Dinner served for fifty cents.' Signed Jacob Jay, minister in charge.

articles.headline: Notice (Ladies' Union Association officers)
articles.summary: 'At a stated meeting of the Ladies' Union Association, the following named persons were elected officers for the ensuing year,' followed by five officers.
people: secretary, Ladies' Union Association (Miss); signs the acknowledgment as S. Lizzie Brown

articles.headline: Acknowledgment (Ladies' Union Association)
articles.author: S. Lizzie Brown
articles.summary: 'The Ladies' Union Association acknowledge with much pleasure, the following donations from Newport, through the efforts of Mrs. M. Haines: From Bethel Mount Zion Church, $7.57 [VERIFY]; Shiloh Baptist, $19; from Friends, $3.12, and one box of fancy articles.' Signed S. Lizzie Brown, Sec'y.

articles.headline: Annual Meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League at Harrisburg, August 9th. Excursion Tickets
articles.author: Jacob C. White, Jr.
articles.summary: 'At half fare, good until the 12th, inclusive. All persons attending the Annual Meeting will purchase tickets, paying full fare, and receive from the Recording Secretary at the Meeting, Return Tickets, Gratis, good on the Pennsylvania Railroad, and on any of its branches, except the Philadelphia & Erie R. R.' By order of the Board.

articles.headline: Notice (Apple Dumpling Festival, A.M.E. Wesley Church)
articles.summary: 'A committee of ladies will give a grand Apple Dumpling Festival, in the basement of the A. M. E. Wesley Church, in Hurst Street, between Fifth and Sixth, and below Lombard street, on Thursday, August 12, 1865, for the benefit of the Church.' Admission 15 cents; tickets at 619 Pine Street. Tagged August 5, 2t.
people: committee, Apple Dumpling Festival, Wesley Church
committee, Apple Dumpling Festival, Wesley Church

articles.headline: Notice (Bishop Wayman's appointments for August)
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: 'Bishop Wayman's appointments for August: Thursday night, 10th, Harrisburg, Pa. Friday night, 11th, Williamsport, Pa. Sabbath, 13th, Buffalo, New York. From thence, God willing, we will travel to the Indiana Conference, at Springfield, Illinois.' Signed W.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Abbie Davis)
articles.author: Rachel Davis
articles.summary: 'Of Abbie Davis, daughter of Rachel Davis, who was born at Wilmington, Delaware. She was carried to Cuba ... over thirty-five years ago.' Later in Texas and New Orleans, where she kept a wash house about 1862. Replies to Rachel Davis, care Christian Recorder, Box 2975, Philadelphia. Tagged Aug. 5, 2t.

articles.headline: Excursion (Macedonia Sabbath School, Camden)
articles.summary: 'The annual excursion of the Macedonia Sabbath School, of Camden, N. J., to Red Bank, will take place on Thursday, August 17, 1865. The steamer Eagle will leave Kaighn's Point at 7 1/2 o'clock, A. M., touching at Philadelphia. Tickets, Adults 40 cents; children half price. They may be had at this office.'
people: committee of arrangements, Macedonia Sabbath School excursion, Camden
committee of arrangements, Macedonia Sabbath School excursion, Camden

articles.headline: Minutes of P. S. E. R. League
articles.author: Jacob C. White, Jr.
articles.summary: 'To members of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, and others interested in the Elective Franchise movement: The Minutes of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights Convention have been ready for some months. Members of the Convention are called upon to redeem their pledges.' Minutes $20 per hundred or 25 cents a copy; Constitutions $5 per hundred or 5 cents. Orders to Jacob C. White, Jr., Sec., 717 Lombard Street, Philadelphia. Tagged July 22, 3t.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Edith Chappel)
articles.summary: 'Edith Chappel left Columbia, South Carolina, on February 20th, 1865, with the army of Gen. Sherman, from the residence of Mrs. Henry Lyons [VERIFY]. Her aunt, Fannie Bostick, can be found with Mr. A. L. Hart, 327 Lombard St., Philadelphia.' Tagged July 22, 2t.
people: aunt of Edith Chappel; to be found with A. L. Hart, 327 Lombard St.

articles.headline: Notice to the Afflicted (Dr. H. S. Phillips; Madam Julian)
articles.summary: 'Dr. H. S. Phillips, Practical Magnetic Physician for Chronic Diseases, has taken rooms at No. 82[?] Race Street, Philadelphia.' 'The services of Madam Julian, a remarkable (and only public colored) Clairvoyant and Trance Medium, have been secured.' Entered as a notice: the doctor is not known to be Black. Tagged July 15, 4t.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: Two marriages at Newport, R.I., July 20, 1865, by Rev. E. T. Williams: Charles Barton to Miss Emily J. Anderson, at the residence of James Palmer; and at the residence of the bride, Mr. Sampson Fay of Jones County, N.C., to Mrs. Harriet Hill of Philadelphia, Pa. [names read on the two-column crop only; VERIFY]

articles.headline: Coal Yard. Thos. J. Bowers
articles.summary: 'Coal Yard. Thos. J. Bowers, (At 634 Lombard Street, above Sixth, Phila.,) has constantly on hand the best Lehigh, Schuylkill and other Coal, at the Lowest Market Price. Coal and Kindling Wood always on hand by small measure.' Orders also received at a number on South Second Street (number not legible). A new, larger ad; the older 'Coal! Coal!!' card of T. J. Bowers (634 Lombard) still runs on page 3.
people: proprietor, coal yard, 634 Lombard Street above Sixth

articles.headline: From Petersburg, Va. (library and Bible from the Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School of Philadelphia)
articles.author: Anna R. Robinson
articles.summary: 'The Library and a handsome Bible were purchased by a society of young ladies attached to the Sabbath School of Shiloh Baptist Church of Philadelphia. The President of the Society, and the Treasurer, brought the articles to this city accompanied by the following address,' dated Philadelphia, July 14th, 1865, to the Gilfield Baptist Church, Petersburg, Va. Signed Anna R. Robinson and Fannie J. Robinson, Petersburg, Va., July 20th, 1865.
people: treasurer, young ladies' society of the Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School; co-signer
vice president, young ladies' society, Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School
secretary, young ladies' society, Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School

articles.headline: Emancipation Celebration at Bath, Penna.
articles.summary: 'A meeting of the colored citizens of Bethlehem was held at Bath, Pa., on the 1st inst., to celebrate the West Indian Emancipation. The following gentlemen were appointed officers for the day: President, Enoch Emory; Vice-President, H. B. Black; Secretary, Wm. N. Stout.' Addresses by Lewis Nicholson, H. B. Black, James H. Wilson and 'the Rev. James H. Smith, of Philadelphia.'
people: of Philadelphia; delivered an address at the Bath celebration (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter from Bro. Seaton
articles.author: D. P. Seaton
articles.summary: Letter from Wilmington, Del., July 29, on the session there of the M. E. Colored Mission Conference and the visit of an A.M.E. Zion delegation; the two bodies agreed to meet in convention in Philadelphia in November.

articles.headline: Letter from the 3d U.S.C.T.
articles.author: Wm. B. Johnson
articles.summary: Letter from Jacksonville, Fla., July 27, 1865, by the Post Clerk, Co. A, on the condition of the Third U.S. Colored Troops (raised at Camp William Penn) and its commander, Brevet Brig. Gen. B. C. Tilghman. No Philadelphia men are named in the part read.

articles.headline: Editorial Correspondence. Sketches by the Wayside
articles.summary: The editor left Philadelphia on Wednesday, August 2, 1865, for the Western conferences, stopping at Pittsburgh (Rev. Samuel Watts; Rev. Lewis Woodson of Allen Chapel) and Cleveland (Rev. John A. Warren).

articles.headline: The City
articles.summary: 'A larger number than usual of our prominent citizens are absent this season from the city; some rusticating among embowered groves, reclining carelessly beside beautiful streams.' Others are at the sea shore. No names given.

articles.headline: Delaware Colored Mission Annual Conference of the M. E. Church
articles.author: Frisby J. Cooper
articles.summary: Journal of a trip through Delaware (July 22-26) and of the conference at Wilmington, Bishop Scott presiding, Bishop A. W. Wayman present. Delegates from the A.M.E. Zion Church (S. T. Jones, Bro. Boslee, S. Golden) visited 'to confer with them on the union of the two bodies'; they decided to hold a convention 'some time in November, 1865, at Zoar Church, Philadelphia.' Appointments, Delaware River District: J. G. Manluff, P. E.; John Wesley Station, A. Brown; Zoar, to be supplied; Camden, J. H. Pearce.

articles.headline: Convention of Colored Men of New Jersey
articles.author: Wm. Steward
articles.summary: 'According to a call issued by the Equal Right's League, of Trenton, N. J., the people of New Jersey (colored) sent delegates, who met in Convention at Trenton, on the 13th of July, (1865,) which, after becoming organized, formed an association styled "The Equal Right's League of New Jersey."' Officers follow. Signed Wm. Steward, Rec. Sec'y.
people: vice president, Equal Rights League of New Jersey; of Burlington (Rev.)

articles.headline: Notice (Apple Dumpling Festival, A.M.E. Wesley Church; date changed)
articles.summary: Same notice as August 5, but the date now reads 'on Monday, August 14, 1865.' Committee printed clearly here: Elizabeth Smith, Amelia J. Spriggs, Ann Hollingsworth. Admission 15 cents; tickets at 619 Pine Street.
people: committee, Apple Dumpling Festival, Wesley Church
committee, Apple Dumpling Festival, Wesley Church
committee, Apple Dumpling Festival, Wesley Church

articles.headline: $25 Reward (John Hunt and Pauline Green)
articles.summary: 'Twenty-five dollars is offered for the arrest of John Hunt or Pauline Green, or both. The latter left her home, at Orange, N. J., with and through the persuasion of the said John Hunt, on the 7th of July last.' She is between 16 and 17; both are colored. Address a woman at Orange, N.J. (name not legible). Compare the Pauline Medora Green notice of August 5 (613 Barclay street, Philadelphia).

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Robinson children, of Fauquier County, Va.)
articles.summary: 'Of Loudon Beckwith, Joseph, and Maria Jane Robinson, children of Samson and Jane Robinson, who came from Fauquier County, Va., about ten years ago.' Information to their sister Eliza Ellen, at Attleborough, Bucks Co., Pa. (surname not legible). Tagged Aug. 12, 3t.

articles.headline: Obituary. Rev. Jeremiah Asher
articles.author: J. H. P.
articles.summary: Dated Head Quarters 27th U.S.C.T., Wilmington, North Carolina, July 30th, 1865. 'Rev. Jeremiah Asher, Chaplain of the 6th U.S.C.T., was attacked by a bilious disease a few weeks ago. ... He died on the 27th of July, 1865.' He 'leaves a dear wife and family'; Mr. and Mrs. Day took him into their own house during his illness, and 'Mr. Day has accompanied the body home to the afflicted wife and friends.'
people: deceased, July 27, 1865, at Wilmington, N.C.; chaplain of the 6th U.S.C.T. (Rev.)

events.name: Ladies' Union Association -- election of officers
events.description: At a stated meeting (date not given; notice printed August 5, 1865) the Ladies' Union Association elected officers for the ensuing year: President, Miss A. E. Mills; Vice President, Miss Amina [VERIFY] Morgan; Secretary, Miss S. L. Brown; Treasurer, Mrs. Elijah Davis; Corresponding Secretary, Miss Carrie R. Lecount. In the same column the Association acknowledges donations from Newport through Mrs. M. Haines (Bethel Mount Zion Church, Shiloh Baptist, Friends, and a box of fancy articles), signed S. Lizzie Brown, Sec'y.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League -- annual meeting called
events.description: Three notices in this issue call the annual meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League at Harrisburg on Wednesday, August 9, 1865, at 10 o'clock (notice dated Philadelphia, July 18, 1865, signed J. C. White, Jr., Sec'y; a display ad; and an excursion-ticket notice signed Jacob C. White, Jr., Secretary, by order of the Board). Delegates pay full fare going and receive free return tickets from the Recording Secretary, good on the Pennsylvania Railroad and branches until the 12th. A fourth notice offers the printed Minutes of the State Equal Rights Convention and the Constitution, from Jacob C. White, Jr., 717 Lombard Street.
attendees: secretary, Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League; 717 Lombard Street (printed 'Jacob C. White, Jr.' and 'J. C. White, Jr.')

events.name: Apple Dumpling Festival, A.M.E. Wesley Church (Hurst Street)
events.location: Basement of the A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street between Fifth and Sixth, below Lombard, Philadelphia
events.description: A committee of ladies announces a grand Apple Dumpling Festival for the benefit of the church. The notice prints 'Thursday, August 12, 1865'; August 12 was a Saturday, so the weekday or the date is a misprint. Committee: Elizabeth Smith, Amelia J. Sprigg [VERIFY], Ann Hollingsworth. Admission 15 cents; tickets for sale at 619 Pine Street.

events.name: Macedonia Sabbath School (Camden) -- annual excursion to Red Bank
events.location: Steamer Eagle from Kaighn's Point, Camden, touching at Philadelphia, to Red Bank
events.description: Annual excursion of the Macedonia Sabbath School of Camden, N.J., to Red Bank on Thursday, August 17, 1865; steamer Eagle leaves Kaighn's Point at 7 1/2 a.m., touching at Philadelphia. Adults 40 cents, children half price; tickets at the Recorder office. Committee of Arrangements: D. G. Harris, O. L. Davis, Mrs. E. Stidham [VERIFY: surname].

events.name: Cape Island (Cape May): colored visitors, the Maria Cornette arrest, and the A.M.E. Quarterly Meeting
events.location: Cape Island, N.J. (United States Hotel; Banneker House; A.M.E. Church)
events.description: Editor Weaver's letter of July 26-31. James Rodgers of Baltimore had Maria Cornette, of Frederick, Md., arrested at the United States Hotel for the alleged theft of a $100 diamond ring; Rev. Stephen Smith went to the Mayor and entered bail, and she was taken to the Banneker House. Mr. Morgan Smith gave a Reading in the A.M.E. Church. On Friday, July 28, Rev. Stephen Smith and family, Mrs. Bishop Wayman, Rev. J. P. Turpin, Mrs. Jordan of Baltimore and the editor visited the farm of Captain Williams. An excursion party of about 300 came from Philadelphia by boat. Sabbath, July 30, Brother Cornish's Quarterly Meeting: the editor preached at 11, Rev. J. P. Turpin at 4, Bishop A. W. Wayman at night.

events.name: Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School (Philadelphia), young ladies' society -- library and Bible presented to Gilfield Baptist Church, Petersburg
events.description: A society (class) of young ladies of the Sabbath School of Shiloh Baptist Church, Philadelphia, bought a library (36 Testaments, 12 hymn-books, 24 reading-books, 60 Union spelling books, 18 primary cards, 225 Sabbath School papers) and a pulpit Bible for the Gilfield Baptist Church; their address is dated Philadelphia, July 14, 1865. Officers as printed: President, Anna R. Robinson; Vice President, Emma E. Freeman; Treasurer, Fannie J. Robinson; Committee, Rebecca Kelly, Sarah Thomas, Eliza Jones, Caroline Thomas, Lauretta West, Julia Freeman, Elizabeth Harris, Virginia Taylor, Emma Kenney [VERIFY]; Secretary, Rebecca S. Cooper. The President and Treasurer carried the gift to Petersburg, where it was presented on Sabbath, July 23, 1865, by Geo. W. Goines, school teacher and missionary there, to a school of over 250 children; the Bible was presented in the afternoon before some 1,200 persons.
attendees: president; carried the gift to Petersburg
treasurer; carried the gift to Petersburg

events.name: First of August (West India Emancipation) celebration at Bath, Pa.
events.description: The colored citizens of Bethlehem met at Bath on August 1, 1865, to celebrate West Indian Emancipation (the 31st anniversary). Officers of the day: President, Enoch Emory; Vice-President, H. B. Black; Secretary, Wm. N. Stout. Lewis Nicholson made the introductory remarks; H. B. Black and James H. Wilson spoke (Wilson on the promotion of colored soldiers and Pennsylvania's duty to give the colored man his rights); 'the Rev. James H. Smith, of Philadelphia,' delivered an address. A collation followed at a hotel. No procession or interference is reported. The Bethlehem men are not linked (outside the Philadelphia area).

events.name: Apple Dumpling Festival, A.M.E. Wesley Church (Hurst Street) -- date now Monday, August 14
events.location: Basement of the A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street between Fifth and Sixth, below Lombard, Philadelphia
events.description: The second insertion of the notice changes the date from 'Thursday, August 12' (August 5 issue) to 'Monday, August 14, 1865.' For the benefit of the church. Committee: Elizabeth Smith, Amelia J. Spriggs, Ann Hollingsworth. Admission 15 cents; tickets at 619 Pine Street.

events.name: Equal Rights League of New Jersey -- formed in convention at Trenton
events.description: On a call of the Equal Rights League of Trenton, colored delegates from across New Jersey met at Trenton on July 13, 1865, and formed 'The Equal Right's League of New Jersey,' adopting a constitution. The city was full of returning soldiers waiting for their pay, but all passed off quietly. Officers for the ensuing year: President, Samuel G. Gould, of Trenton; Vice Presidents, Rev. Theodore Gould and Robert Prim [VERIFY], both of Burlington; Recording Secretary, William Steward, of Bridgeton, Cumberland Co.; Corresponding Secretary, Rev. Reading B. Johns, of Princeton; Treasurer, Abijah Gould, Jr., of Bridgeton. Delegates to the National League in September: the President and Rev. N. H. Turpin, of Salem, N.J. 500 copies of the minutes to be had of the Recording Secretary at $15 per hundred.

events.name: M. E. Colored Mission Conference and A.M.E. Zion delegates -- union convention appointed for Zoar Church, Philadelphia
events.location: Wilmington, Del. (convention to be held at Zoar Church, Philadelphia, November 1865)
events.description: At the Delaware Colored Mission Annual Conference of the M. E. Church at Wilmington (Bishop Scott presiding), delegates of the A.M.E. Zion Church (S. T. Jones, Bro. Boslee and S. Golden) conferred on the union of the two bodies. It was decided to hold a convention 'some time in November, 1865, at Zoar Church, Philadelphia,' of four delegates from each annual conference; the conference appointed James Davis, Wilmore S. Elsey, Harrison Smith and John G. Manluff. Appointments, Delaware River District: J. G. Manluff, presiding elder; John Wesley Station, A. Brown; Zoar, to be supplied; Camden, J. H. Pearce; Salem, N. Young. Reported by Frisby J. Cooper. None linked (M. E. clergy of the Delaware conference).

events.name: Death of Rev. Jeremiah Asher, chaplain of the 6th U.S.C.T.
events.description: Rev. Jeremiah Asher, chaplain of the 6th U.S. Colored Troops (and pastor of Shiloh Baptist Church, Philadelphia, though the obituary does not say so), died of a bilious disease at Wilmington, N.C., on July 27, 1865, after some weeks' illness in the house of Mr. and Mrs. Day. Mr. Day accompanied the body home to his wife and friends. Reported from Head Quarters 27th U.S.C.T., July 30, by 'J. H. P.'
